audit.whatIsWrong: The matchup treats Vault (E) as a combined dash-and-blind ('Vault (Dash/Blind)' in focus.text, loading, winCon and eight report/breakdown strings), and whys[1], early and spikes[0].text all describe Vault blinding Ryze. Vault does not blind. The blind is Blinding Assault (Q, 11/10.5/10/9.5/9s, 1025 range), a separate ability — and a blind stops basic attacks, which is not how Ryze deals damage at all.
audit.why: Riot's text for Vault: 'Quinn dashes to an enemy, dealing physical damage and slowing the target's Move Speed. Upon reaching the target, she leaps off the target, briefly interrupting it, and lands near her maximum Attack Range away.' It is a 12/11/10/9/8s disengage with a brief interrupt, not a blind. Overload, Rune Prison and Spell Flux are all spell damage, so Blinding Assault costs Ryze nothing except the vision hinder. Also unstated: Behind Enemy Lines is a channel, so Rune Prison (615, 11-9s) cancels it outright.
audit.corrected: Vault is the 8-12s dash-away with a brief interrupt; Blinding Assault is the separate blind, and it does not stop your spells. Rune Prison cancels Behind Enemy Lines.

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet defect: 'level chart contradicts data — Ryze wins 58.22% but the chart gives Quinn 6/7 stages vs 1'. Disk currently reads Skill / Quinn / Quinn / Skill / Skill / Quinn / Quinn, which contradicts the packet in a different way and also contradicts whys[6] and the late paragraph, both of which say two items flips the lane to Ryze.
audit.why: The mirror settled it: rows 0, 3 and 4 to Quinn, row 6 to Ryze, as one atomic group. That gives Quinn the lane and Ryze the game, which is exactly what the late text and the 58.22% win rate together describe — you lose lane and win the game.
audit.corrected: Quinn / Quinn / Quinn / Quinn / Quinn / Quinn / Ryze, as matched full+content pairs with ratings adjusted.

audit.why: Four spikes present: Lvl 1-5 (Vault denies every entry), Lvl 6 (her roam peak), 1st item (her crit item lands first), 2+ items (Rod of Ages plus Seraph's). Ryze's only owned window is the last, matching the corrected chart.
audit.corrected: Spike timings untouched; spikes[0].text reworded for the Vault error and phases[4].why rewritten for its new side.

edits.after: Vault (E) negates your W-root setup: she leaps off you the instant you commit, briefly interrupts you, lands at her attack range, and gets a free Harrier proc.

edits.before: Quinn's Vault (E) knocks you back and applies a blind, completely shutting down your ability to walk up and Flux-stack — she controls every trade window through mid-lane.
edits.after: Quinn's Vault (E) leaps off you and lands her back at attack range, shutting down your ability to walk up and Flux-stack — she controls every trade window through mid-lane.

edits.before: Quinn's Vault (E) is the entire lane problem from level 1: the moment you step up to E-Flux her she vaults away, blinds you, and the auto-attacks you cannot land during blind mean your empowered Q lands for nothing. Do not try to force the Flux chain in the open — instead E the minion adjacent to her to bounce Flux onto her without closing distance, then W-root only if the bounce connects. Accept that levels 1 through 3 are about stacking Manaflow Band charges and Tear of the Goddess, not winning trades.
edits.after: Quinn's Vault (E) is the entire lane problem from level 1: the moment you step up to E-Flux her she leaps off you, interrupts the cast, and lands at her own attack range, so your empowered Q chases someone already gone. Do not try to force the Flux chain in the open — instead E the minion adjacent to her to bounce Flux onto her without closing distance, then W-root only if the bounce connects. Accept that levels 1 through 3 are about stacking Manaflow Band charges and Tear of the Goddess, not winning trades.

edits.before: Blind + disengage in one button — fight while it is down. Bait it, count it, then go.
edits.after: Vault is the disengage on 8-12s; the blind is a separate Q. Fight on that gap.

notes: Second-biggest find of the slice: 'Vault (Dash/Blind)' fuses two different abilities and then builds advice on the fused version. Vault is the dash-away with a brief interrupt; Blinding Assault is the blind, and a blind is nearly worthless against a champion whose damage is entirely spells. focus.text and the loading string still carry the fused label — re-keying them changes the matchup's whole framing and the mirror did not touch it either, so I flagged it rather than doing it unilaterally (see questionsForUser).
